name: block-frames
description: The anchor for the rule a block is framed with, and for the category a verse takes its own type and frame from. The renderer STROKES a frame on the block's bounds — half of it outside, none of it inside — and measures the padding from that same edge, so the rule costs the block neither height nor content width; a CSS border costs it both, which made every framed block a rule-width taller and its text a rule-width further in. And a verse is not a quotation: the gem's default theme gives `verse` a category of its own whose `$quote_*` defaults are frozen at the DEFAULT theme's quote values when that file loads, so a project that restyles `quote` does not restyle `verse` — which is why this fixture's theme sets every quote value away from the renderer's own.
